children: Asian equities face renewed selling pressure Monday as an investigation involving Nvidia
Chief Executive Jensen Huang threatens to deepen a global technology stock downturn, Bloomberg News reported.

into whether Huang was targeted in an alleged Chinese espionage operation. U.S. authorities suspect former Megaspeed International executive Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence. A blockchain-based futures contract tracking Nvidia shares declined following the news.

For investors, the investigation introduces another source of uncertainty for the artificial intelligence industry, which has helped drive equity valuations worldwide. Nvidia's central role in AI infrastructure makes developments involving its leadership particularly consequential for semiconductor stocks and broader technology markets.

The investigation follows a difficult week for global equities. Technology stocks led a selloff that pushed Japanese and Taiwanese markets into bear-market territory, generally defined as declines of at least 20% from recent peaks. A global stock benchmark fell to a six-month low.
Investors are also monitoring geopolitical tensions after a Houthi attack damaged property in Riyadh's financial district, including offices belonging to Saudi Aramco (
). Meanwhile, China's consumer and producer inflation figures, due Monday, could provide fresh evidence of the country's economic outlook. The dollar
was mixed against major currencies after gaining 0.4% last week, while Bitcoin traded near $75,000.
